Hannopil Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Khmelnytskyi Oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. This record shows a tension worth noting: it is categorized as 'fenced and protected,' yet the source's demolished field marks it as 'yes.' Hannopil holds one of the most significant sites in this collection: Dov Ber ben Avraham of Mezeritch — the Maggid of Mezritch, successor to the Baal Shem Tov and a figure whose students are documented at Tulchyn and Zboriv elsewhere in this collection — lived here with his son Avraham (1741–1776), known as 'Ha-Malach' (the Angel), who later became a tzaddik in Fastiv. Rabbi Shneur-Zalman of Liady, founder of Chabad-Lubavitch Hasidism, also stayed here for a time. The Maggid's disciple Meshulam-Zusya Annopolsky (died 1800), who made a major contribution to spreading Hasidism throughout Volhynia, settled and was buried here, and his son Zvi-Menachem-Mendl (died 1814) became the town's Admor after him. This cemetery was destroyed during WWII, but the graves of Dov Ber ben Avraham and Meshulam-Zusi Zvi-Menachem-Mendl were reconstructed in 1988; the site is now a Hasidic pilgrimage destination with an adjacent visitor center, protected by the Ohalei Tzadikim — Gader Avot union, documented at several other sites in this collection. In January 1942, Hannopil's Jewish community, along with Jews from neighboring villages, was sent to Slavuta and executed there on June 26, 1942.
